chapters.title: The Beginning
chapters.arc: Wonder gives way to broken trust; David learns that force cannot repair every loss.

chapters.title: The Promise
chapters.arc: A journey begins without a complete map; Ken learns patience alongside David.

chapters.title: The Divided Family
chapters.arc: Betrayal, exile and famine make forgiveness a costly choice.

chapters.title: Out of Egypt
chapters.arc: Oppression meets deliverance; the friends protect people instead of chasing revenge.

chapters.title: A People and a Land
chapters.arc: Law, worship and wilderness test whether courage can wait and listen.

chapters.title: Courage in Dark Days
chapters.arc: Deliverers rise; small acts of loyalty matter alongside great feats.

chapters.title: The First Kings
chapters.arc: Leadership and appearance diverge; mercy becomes harder than victory.

chapters.title: A Kingdom Divided
chapters.arc: Songs, wisdom and splintering power show the limits of strength.

chapters.title: Voices in the Storm
chapters.arc: Prophets call people back; judgment and promised restoration are held together.

chapters.title: Exile and Return
chapters.arc: Faithfulness survives far from home; rebuilding takes shared effort.

chapters.title: The Promised Arrival
chapters.arc: Waiting gives way to birth, preparation and the beginning of Jesus’ ministry.

chapters.title: The Kingdom Comes Near
chapters.arc: Teaching, mercy and signs reshape what the friends think greatness means.

chapters.title: Mercy and Truth
chapters.arc: Healing and welcome lead toward Jerusalem and the coming cost.

chapters.title: The Cross and the Empty Tomb
chapters.arc: Weapons are put away; sorrow gives way to the resurrection announcement.

levels.title: Light over the Waters
levels.location: creation panorama: water, sky, green slopes
levels.storyBeat: David and Ken open the Story Archive and watch the ordered creation unfold.
levels.objective: Reach three observation terraces and assemble six illustrated day panels.
levels.uniqueRule: Platforms appear only after the narration beat; the player neither creates the world nor controls God.

levels.title: The Garden Paths
levels.location: river garden with four branching paths
levels.storyBeat: The friends discover work, companionship and the goodness of the garden before the fracture.
levels.objective: Find four context markers and guide Ken back to the central path.
levels.uniqueRule: Follow river sounds with equivalent directional captions; no combat, forbidden-fruit collecting or speculative map of Eden.

levels.title: The Broken Choice
levels.location: garden threshold, dusk and thorned outer path
levels.storyBeat: The biblical choice is shown as a fixed account; David wonders why winning is not the same as choosing well.
levels.objective: Match three cause-and-consequence panels and leave by the open path.
levels.uniqueRule: No alternate ending prevents the Fall; the serpent is a story figure, never a grindable loot boss.

levels.title: My Brother’s Keeper
levels.location: fictional archive road beside the Cain-and-Abel context panels
levels.storyBeat: Ken asks what responsibility for another person looks like after the account of Cain and Abel.
levels.objective: Escort three frightened archive travelers to separate safe gates.
levels.uniqueRule: The historical murder is a restrained narrated scene; no player input harms Abel and no score rewards revenge.

levels.title: The Ark Workshop
levels.location: fictional carpentry exercise outside an ark exhibit
levels.storyBeat: Noah’s obedience becomes the chapter’s first practical teamwork challenge.
levels.objective: Complete three supply deliveries while clearing three waves of fictional training raiders.
levels.uniqueRule: Carry planks with attacks disabled; set them down safely, defend Ken, then resume building. The raiders are invented.

levels.title: Through the Flood
levels.location: ark walkway and covenant overlook
levels.storyBeat: David learns that the flood and the covenant belong to the biblical narrative, not to his combat skill.
levels.objective: Secure three loose cargo latches and reach the post-flood observation deck.
levels.uniqueRule: Water rises along an authored safe route; no fight against God, no survival score claims to cause the covenant.

levels.title: The Scattered Tower
levels.location: unfinished brick terraces of Babel
levels.storyBeat: Confusion scatters the crowd; the friends must help people without a shared language.
levels.objective: Use pictogram signs to reconnect four routes and reach the archive exit.
levels.uniqueRule: Routes split after a fixed story cue; instructions use shapes and captions instead of making any language a villain.

levels.title: A Road without a Map
levels.location: Abram’s road, tents and ochre ridges
levels.storyBeat: Abram’s call starts the promise arc; David protects a fictional travel exercise.
levels.objective: Escort a supply cart through three gates and clear the road-raider waves.
levels.uniqueRule: The cart waits in safe bays while combat runs, preventing simultaneous damage and unreadable escort pressure.

levels.title: The Rescue of Lot
levels.location: night ridge, camp outskirts and release corridor
levels.storyBeat: The account of Abram rescuing Lot anchors an archive rescue challenge.
levels.objective: Open two captive gates and clear the final guard wave before returning to Ken.
levels.uniqueRule: Two lanes let the player flank archers; rescued people remain in invulnerable safe zones after release.

levels.title: Stars beyond Counting
levels.location: quiet night overlook and star-panel mosaic
levels.storyBeat: Ken admits that promises can seem too large to believe; the story pauses beneath the stars.
levels.objective: Arrange four promise-and-context panels and activate the route marker.
levels.uniqueRule: Stars are scenery, never experience points, divine energy or a currency purchased by faith.

levels.title: The Mountain of Provision
levels.location: mountain approach and restrained observation terrace
levels.storyBeat: The account of Abraham and Isaac is presented with care, ending with God’s provision.
levels.objective: Walk the approach, view three context cards and continue after the narrated outcome.
levels.uniqueRule: No button raises a blade against a child, no sacrifice mini-game, no boss or alternate outcome.

levels.title: Water at the Well
levels.location: well court, troughs and shaded caravan rest
levels.storyBeat: Rebekah’s hospitality gives David a challenge built on service rather than speed alone.
levels.objective: Carry water to three troughs and guide the caravan to a shaded rest point.
levels.uniqueRule: Water weight changes carrying animation only; no gender-based stat changes or fabricated miracle.

levels.title: A Stairway in the Night
levels.location: stone sleeping place and dream observation panels
levels.storyBeat: Jacob’s dream opens a new family chapter while Ken questions whether the road can still lead home.
levels.objective: Reach three dream-view terraces and return to the waking camp marker.
levels.uniqueRule: The dream is a fixed narrated vision; David’s jumps do not climb into heaven or earn access to God.

levels.title: The Long Walk to Esau
levels.location: river ford and open reunion field
levels.storyBeat: Jacob prepares to meet Esau; the reunion shifts the friends from fear toward reconciliation.
levels.objective: Deliver three message tokens and choose a peaceful route through the exercise.
levels.uniqueRule: Jacob’s wrestling is narrated without making God or an angel a health-bar boss; Esau is not an enemy to defeat.

levels.title: The Torn Coat
levels.location: fictional training canyon beside Joseph’s context gallery
levels.storyBeat: Joseph’s betrayal is fixed history; David cannot erase it, but he can protect others in a separate exercise.
levels.objective: Protect Ken while retrieving three torn archive pages through raider waves.
levels.uniqueRule: Pages are contextual collectibles, never pieces whose recovery prevents Joseph’s sale; keep historical and invented panels distinct.

levels.title: Integrity in the House
levels.location: house corridors and clearly marked exit balconies
levels.storyBeat: Joseph’s integrity and unjust imprisonment are summarized without reenacting sexual coercion.
levels.objective: Find the lawful exit route and reach the witness panel.
levels.uniqueRule: Close doors and use line-of-sight hiding; no seduction choices, victim blame or combat against the historical accuser.

levels.title: Beyond the Prison Gate
levels.location: fictional prison-yard training arena with two low ledges
levels.storyBeat: The prison account introduces patient service; an invented Gate Warden tests David’s timing.
levels.objective: Ring out the Gate Warden and carry a message to Ken.
levels.uniqueRule: A visible key-ring tell announces shield charges; waiting for recovery is more effective than repeated heavy attacks.

boss.name: Gate Warden
phases: Shield advance: a 36-tick raised-key tell precedes a low charge; jump over it and punish 32 recovery ticks.
At 65% guard, alternate a vertical key-chain swing and a short shield rush; each locks its facing before active contact.
At 30% guard, use charge–pause–swing with a full 42-tick recovery. No added enemies; the boss remains one readable threat.

levels.title: Bread for the Hungry
levels.location: fictional grain-yard obstacle arena and family reunion gallery
levels.storyBeat: Famine brings Joseph’s family together; forgiveness resolves the family chapter.
levels.objective: Outmaneuver the invented Grain Hoarder, then distribute three supply bundles.
levels.uniqueRule: The boss blocks routes with sacks, not divine famine; the reunion is fixed and never conditional on a perfect score.

boss.name: Grain Hoarder
phases: Sack toss: mark the landing lane for 42 ticks; move to the opposite low platform.
At 65% guard, push a rolling model sack across the floor with a jumpable gap and 36 recovery ticks.
At 30% guard, use toss then push; remove old hazards before the next sequence. Punish from above.

levels.title: A Basket on the River
levels.location: Nile-bank reeds and stone footpaths
levels.storyBeat: Moses’ early account begins the deliverance chapter; Ken learns to move gently under pressure.
levels.objective: Guide an observation skiff along three safe shoreline markers.
levels.uniqueRule: The historical infant is never a damageable escort entity; the moving object is a fictional archive model.

levels.title: The Burning Bush
levels.location: desert approach, distant bush and quiet observation circle
levels.storyBeat: Moses receives his call; the friends listen before the road back to Egypt opens.
levels.objective: Reach the viewpoint, read two context cards and confirm Continue.
levels.uniqueRule: No harvesting fire, weaponizing the bush, invented words spoken as God, or claiming an exact visual form for God.

levels.title: A Hard-Hearted Court
levels.location: fictional court drill outside the palace history panel
levels.storyBeat: Oppression and the plagues are narrated; David faces an invented Court Warden in a separate exercise.
levels.objective: Break the warden’s guard and guide Ken through the exit lane.
levels.uniqueRule: The boss’s guard mechanic never represents Pharaoh’s heart or causes a plague; God’s acts remain fixed story events.

boss.name: Court Warden
phases: Spear lane: a 36-tick shoulder draw precedes a straight thrust; duck to a lower route or dodge through the active interval.
At 65% guard, alternate a shield shove and an overhead strike with distinct poses.
At 30% guard, combine shove and thrust with a clearly visible reset; punish the 40-tick end lag.

levels.title: The Passover Night
levels.location: quiet household exhibit and departure courtyard
levels.storyBeat: The Passover prepares the exodus; the pace becomes solemn and attentive.
levels.objective: Arrange departure supplies, read the historical context and reach the waiting families.
levels.uniqueRule: No timed door-marking that decides a child’s death, no collectible plague victims, no combat or celebratory casualty score.

levels.title: The Path through the Sea
levels.location: open seabed path with distant water walls
levels.storyBeat: God’s deliverance opens a way; the friends follow an archive route through the account.
levels.objective: Reach three safe route markers and join Ken at the far shore.
levels.uniqueRule: The sea opens on the authored narrative cue; the player does not unlock the miracle with damage or command the drowning.

levels.title: Water, Bread and Battle
levels.location: fictional wilderness defensive exercise and separate provision panels
levels.storyBeat: Provision and the Amalek battle show dependence and shared effort.
levels.objective: Defend three supply bays from fictional raiders and reach the closing account panel.
levels.uniqueRule: Rotate lanes between waves; water and manna are narrative gifts, never healing spells cast by Moses in combat.

levels.title: A Covenant at Sinai
levels.location: mountain-foot camp with scroll-card stations
levels.storyBeat: The people hear the covenant commands; David learns that clear boundaries make life together possible.
levels.objective: Visit four context stations and place an illustrated command summary in the journal.
levels.uniqueRule: No combat on the sacred mountain, no boss representing God, no quiz failure portrayed as loss of salvation.

levels.title: A Place to Gather
levels.location: tabernacle-workshop exhibit outside the worship enclosure
levels.storyBeat: Shared craftsmanship gives the friends a constructive challenge.
levels.objective: Sort four material bundles and finish three model-workshop stations.
levels.uniqueRule: The model is explicitly educational; sacred objects stay behind the history panel and are never pickups or weapons.

levels.title: The Spies’ Report
levels.location: fictional ridge arena beside the scouts’ context panels
levels.storyBeat: Fear spreads after the report; David faces a towering training Ridge Sentinel.
levels.objective: Dodge the sentinel’s lane sweeps and ring it out.
levels.uniqueRule: The sentinel is an invented obstacle, not an ethnic caricature of a Canaanite or a substitute for the canonical outcome.

boss.name: Ridge Sentinel
phases: Wide sweep: 42-tick windup, horizontal contact, 36-tick whiff recovery; jump to the center shelf.
At 65% guard, add a marked descending strike. The marker follows no target during its last 18 ticks.
At 30% guard, alternate sweep and descending strike. Keep a 48-tick punish window after the pair.

levels.title: Look and Live
levels.location: wilderness paths and a distant observation standard
levels.storyBeat: The bronze-serpent account is summarized as deliverance, not a collectible power-up.
levels.objective: Guide Ken along three marked safe paths and view the context panel.
levels.uniqueRule: No player creates healing through a timing combo; no sacred standard can be picked up, traded or thrown.

levels.title: Stones from the Jordan
levels.location: river crossing exhibit and memorial-stone shore
levels.storyBeat: Crossing the Jordan opens the land chapter; remembering matters as much as arriving.
levels.objective: Carry three illustrative memorial tokens to their slots and reach the shore.
levels.uniqueRule: The crossing is a fixed narrative act; the educational tokens do not claim to be the historical twelve stones.

levels.title: Around the Walls
levels.location: fictional outskirts training course, distant Jericho history view
levels.storyBeat: The Jericho account closes the chapter; the friends rehearse discipline around an outside course.
levels.objective: Complete a perimeter route and clear three training waves outside the historical scene.
levels.uniqueRule: Trumpets are context audio, not damage projectiles; the wall falls in narration rather than after a boss health bar empties.

levels.title: Under Deborah’s Palm
levels.location: palm-court drill with alternating upper lanes
levels.storyBeat: Deborah and Barak’s account opens a chapter of courage amid instability.
levels.objective: Protect two regroup points and defeat three mixed training waves.
levels.uniqueRule: A captain signals which lane will attack; Deborah’s leadership is contextual and not a supernatural stat buff.

levels.title: The Call of Gideon
levels.location: threshing-floor exhibit and camp preparation route
levels.storyBeat: Gideon’s call makes room for uncertainty and patient preparation.
levels.objective: Place three context panels in order and prepare two camp stations.
levels.uniqueRule: No prayer button buys evidence or power; fleece events remain narrated, with no invented instructions attributed to God.

levels.title: Three Hundred Lanterns
levels.location: fictional night training ridge with light and cover lanes
levels.storyBeat: The account of Gideon’s reduced force becomes a lesson in coordinated timing.
levels.objective: Trigger three visual camp signals and clear three training waves.
levels.uniqueRule: Lantern signals open safe routes; enemy confusion in Scripture is not explained as a player-owned magic attack.

levels.title: The Lion on the Road
levels.location: rock road with a low central shelf
levels.storyBeat: Samson’s lion account becomes a clearly stylized sporting encounter in the archive.
levels.objective: Evade the Lion’s pounce and complete the three opening windows.
levels.uniqueRule: Avoid gore and eating-from-carcass gameplay; the historical context and the invented multi-phase drill are labeled separately.

boss.name: Lion drill
phases: Pounce: 42-tick crouch tell, fixed leap endpoint, 36-tick recovery; sidestep then counter the training opening.
After the first opening, add a short ground dash with dust and caption cues; no invisible hit from the tail.
After the second opening, use feint–pounce; one stable platform remains safe. The third opening ends the drill without gore.

levels.title: The Gates of Gaza
levels.location: fictional gate-carry training yard with ramps
levels.storyBeat: Strength is spectacular, but Ken begins to question what it is for.
levels.objective: Defeat the invented Gate Captain, then carry a training gate frame to the ridge.
levels.uniqueRule: Samson’s canonical gate feat is shown separately; gate-carry input does not grant unlimited strength or sacred power.

boss.name: Gate Captain
phases: Mallet slam: 42-tick windup with a marked floor lane; leave the marker and punish 36 recovery ticks.
At 65% guard, two slow lane sweeps arrive from alternating sides; no helper enemies.
At 30% guard, slam then leap to the marked center; punish the landing recovery before the carry section starts.

levels.title: Grain in the Field
levels.location: harvest field, gleaning lanes and town approach
levels.storyBeat: Ruth’s loyalty ends the chapter with ordinary care and restored hope.
levels.objective: Gather three gleaning bundles and escort two travelers to the town gate.
levels.uniqueRule: This is an interlude set during the judges, not an asserted date after Samson; no combat against farmers or reward for hoarding.

levels.title: A Voice in the Night
levels.location: Shiloh context gallery and quiet sleeping-room exhibit
levels.storyBeat: Hannah and Samuel introduce listening before leadership.
levels.objective: Read three illustrated context cards and follow the sound-caption markers.
levels.uniqueRule: No attack inside a worship scene; distinguish narrator paraphrase from any licensed Scripture quotation.

levels.title: The King the People Wanted
levels.location: fictional muster field outside a Saul history gallery
levels.storyBeat: Saul’s beginning shows the attraction and responsibility of kingship.
levels.objective: Defend two rally standards through three mixed training waves.
levels.uniqueRule: Standards are drill markers, not sacred relics; no kingship unlock grants higher combat stats than the roster budget.

levels.title: Jonathan’s Narrow Climb
levels.location: two narrow cliff routes and a broad top arena
levels.storyBeat: Jonathan’s courage gives David a vertical challenge with limited safe resting space.
levels.objective: Climb to the ridge, clear three guard waves and open the return route.
levels.uniqueRule: Telegraph attacks before narrow jumps; do not equate the opponent’s national identity with moral worth.

levels.title: The Shepherd’s Courage
levels.location: fictional shepherd training terrace and animal encounter exhibit
levels.storyBeat: David’s recollection of protecting sheep prepares the encounter with Goliath.
levels.objective: Protect the model flock and outmaneuver the Bear training encounter.
levels.uniqueRule: This is an explicit lookback within David’s account; the model sheep are never killed or used as bait.

boss.name: Bear drill
phases: Swat: 36-tick shoulder rise, short contact, 36-tick recovery; stay beyond the visible paw envelope.
After the first opening, alternate a low rush and standing swat; protect the model-flock lane by flanking.
After the second opening, the rush stops at a fixed marker and exposes the back. Clear the third opening; no killing animation.

levels.title: David and Goliath
levels.location: broad Elah approach, stream-stone bay and giant’s lane
levels.storyBeat: A giant’s challenge meets David’s trust; the archive presents the decisive account carefully.
levels.objective: As David in this special reenactment, collect a stone, avoid the giant’s attacks and complete one decisive aim opportunity.
levels.uniqueRule: Use composure stages before the shot, not repeated head-hit damage phases. One successful stone resolves the narrated defeat; omit graphic aftermath.

boss.name: Goliath
phases: Approach: avoid three strongly telegraphed spear lanes while reaching the stream-stone bay; no health chip.
Composure: after collecting one stone, avoid two shield advances until Goliath pauses. The aim button becomes available at that visible pause.
Decisive shot: aim within a generous marked opening and release one stone. A missed attempt resets the composure stage; a hit transitions immediately to the restrained narrated outcome.

levels.title: Mercy in the Cave
levels.location: cave chambers with shadow bands and a safe outer exit
levels.storyBeat: David spares Saul; David discovers that having an opening does not mean taking a violent advantage.
levels.objective: Reach the context marker and return unseen to the cave exit.
levels.uniqueRule: Saul has no player-targetable hurtbox; the completion condition is restraint, never killing him.

levels.title: The Procession to Jerusalem
levels.location: city approach, procession path and context panels
levels.storyBeat: The ark’s arrival is narrated reverently; the friends help direct a fictional crowd exercise outside it.
levels.objective: Guide three crowd groups to open lanes and reach the observation terrace.
levels.uniqueRule: The ark is not a weapon, movable player object or boss; difficult details are contextualized without a slapstick failure scene.

levels.title: A Song in the Wilderness
levels.location: quiet psalm gallery with valley and return-home motifs
levels.storyBeat: Poetry makes room for trust and repentance between the kingship episodes.
levels.objective: Pair four illustrated themes with original paraphrase cards.
levels.uniqueRule: This is a thematic interlude, not a claim about the precise dates or locations of these psalms; no rhythm score measures faith.

levels.title: The Wisdom of a King
levels.location: judgment-hall observation exhibit
levels.storyBeat: Solomon’s request for wisdom and the judgment account deepen the distinction between cleverness and care.
levels.objective: Identify the two context clues in a nonviolent panel puzzle.
levels.uniqueRule: A child is never threatened by player input; the account is narrated and no fake trial decides the canonical result.

levels.title: Building the Temple
levels.location: fictional stone-yard exercise outside a temple exhibit
levels.storyBeat: Construction and dedication offer a grand visual midpoint.
levels.objective: Protect three material deliveries from training raiders, then watch the dedication summary.
levels.uniqueRule: Combat remains in the fictional quarry yard; no attack inside the temple and no sacred furnishing becomes a pickup.

levels.title: A Kingdom in Pieces
levels.location: forked training road between two history panels
levels.storyBeat: The kingdom divides; Ken sees how harsh decisions can fracture a community.
levels.objective: Protect two exits through three coordinated training waves.
levels.uniqueRule: Both sides of the historic divide receive context; no game-wide ethnic, regional or religious faction is made inherently evil.

levels.title: Fire and a Quiet Voice
levels.location: fictional mountain-edge drill beside the Elijah gallery
levels.storyBeat: Elijah’s confrontation and flight lead from public spectacle into weariness and renewed calling.
levels.objective: Evade the invented Pursuer Captain and reach the refuge panel.
levels.uniqueRule: Fire and the later voice are narrative events, never Elijah’s repeatable combat spell; no player sets the miracle’s success chance.

boss.name: Pursuer Captain
phases: Javelin: 42-tick raised-arm tell, fixed marked trajectory, 36 recovery ticks; cross underneath after release.
At 65% guard, add a lunging sweep after the javelin; retain a high safe platform.
At 30% guard, use two alternating throws then a long exposed recovery; no fire, miracle or sacred item attack.

levels.title: A River and a Return
levels.location: riverbank paths and Naaman context exhibit
levels.storyBeat: Naaman’s account turns attention toward humility and receiving help.
levels.objective: Collect three context clues and guide Ken along the river route.
levels.uniqueRule: The healing is fixed narration; do not make washing a medical simulator or healing a reward for a perfect jump sequence.

levels.title: The Runaway Prophet
levels.location: ship-deck exhibit, shore route and Nineveh overlook
levels.storyBeat: Jonah’s story presses the friends to consider mercy beyond their preferred people.
levels.objective: Secure three model-deck ropes, follow the shore path and view the mercy ending.
levels.uniqueRule: The great fish is never a boss to kill or a magic mount; the text’s sequence stays intact and the book’s exact date is not asserted.

levels.title: A Promise through Isaiah
levels.location: prophetic scroll gallery with dawn and suffering motifs
levels.storyBeat: Isaiah’s passages widen the promise beyond present distress.
levels.objective: Visit three contextual reading stations and save their references in the journal.
levels.uniqueRule: No invented prophecy, date prediction or magic-scroll attack. Distinguish later Christian interpretation from a fabricated scene witnessed by David.

levels.title: The Siege at the Gate
levels.location: fictional outer-wall defensive drill and refuge yard
levels.storyBeat: Hezekiah’s crisis raises the stakes; the friends protect people while deliverance remains God’s act in the account.
levels.objective: Hold three refuge approaches through shield-and-archer training waves.
levels.uniqueRule: The player does not kill the historical army to cause deliverance; the drill is separate and avoids graphic casualty counts.

levels.title: The Book Found Again
levels.location: repair workshop, scroll archive and city route
levels.storyBeat: Josiah hears the recovered book; the friends learn why remembering can demand change.
levels.objective: Find three archive labels and return a model scroll to the safe reading desk.
levels.uniqueRule: The book is a context exhibit, not an upgrade scroll; no points certify someone’s repentance.

levels.title: Hope in Exile
levels.location: fictional refugee training route beside the fall-and-exile gallery
levels.storyBeat: Jerusalem’s fall ends the kingdom arc, while Jeremiah’s promises preserve hope.
levels.objective: Defeat the invented Siege Captain and escort Ken to the archive shelter.
levels.uniqueRule: The defensive success cannot prevent the recorded exile; do not show player victory as rewriting Jeremiah or erasing suffering.

boss.name: Siege Captain
phases: Shield rush: 42-tick flag tell, locked lane, 36-tick recovery; jump behind and counter.
At 65% guard, an overhead slam marks a different lane for 42 ticks; keep the refugee bay untargetable.
At 30% guard, alternate rush and slam without adds; a 48-tick recovery opens the final punish. The historical exile still follows.

levels.title: Faithful in a Foreign Court
levels.location: Babylonian court classroom exhibit
levels.storyBeat: Daniel and his companions begin the exile chapter with a choice about faithfulness.
levels.objective: Sort three account panels and navigate the classroom route.
levels.uniqueRule: The food account is context, never a real-world health claim or a diet stat bonus.

levels.title: The Furnace Witness
levels.location: safe observation route around a furnace exhibit
levels.storyBeat: The three companions’ deliverance is presented as God’s action amid coercion.
levels.objective: Reach two observation stations and help Ken through an external ember obstacle course.
levels.uniqueRule: The historical companions have no depleting life bars; David cannot extinguish the furnace to save them. No exact identity is forced onto the fourth figure beyond the text.

levels.title: The Lions’ Den
levels.location: restrained den observation exhibit and dawn exit
levels.storyBeat: The lions’ den account continues the theme of faithfulness under threat.
levels.objective: Visit the context marker and walk to the dawn viewpoint.
levels.uniqueRule: No fighting or farming lions, no player rescue that replaces God’s deliverance, no timed button that determines Daniel’s fate.

levels.title: The First Return
levels.location: fictional rubble-clearing yard beside the rebuilding account
levels.storyBeat: Return and rebuilding move the friends from endurance toward shared work.
levels.objective: Complete three repair stations while defending materials from training raiders.
levels.uniqueRule: Ezra’s temple rebuilding is placed before the Esther interlude in this broad historical sequence; no claimed exact date for every archive exercise.

levels.title: For Such a Time
levels.location: fictional palace-garden drill and court-story observation room
levels.storyBeat: Esther’s courage leads into a dangerous appeal; Ken learns that careful speech can protect people.
levels.objective: Pass two dialogue checkpoints, defeat an invented Court Warden in the separate drill and view the account’s resolution.
levels.uniqueRule: The warden is not Haman; Esther’s appeal succeeds in fixed narration, not through a sword duel or magical royal favor.

boss.name: Court Warden
phases: Cross-court thrust: 42-tick shoulder tell and a locked straight lane; dodge late and punish 36 recovery ticks.
At 65% guard, add a fan-shaped shield sweep with a safe upper ledge; no magic fan or charm effect.
At 30% guard, use thrust–sweep then 48 recovery ticks; the historical appeal proceeds through narration after the separate exercise.

levels.title: Builders under Watch
levels.location: wall-work training court with three work bays
levels.storyBeat: Rebuilding Jerusalem closes the exile-and-return chapter with teamwork.
levels.objective: Protect three builders’ bays through four mixed training waves and deliver the final model stone.
levels.uniqueRule: Each cleared bay becomes permanently safe; workers cannot die offscreen, and the victory acknowledges shared work.

levels.title: The Long Wait
levels.location: promise gallery opening into a first-century road
levels.storyBeat: The friends revisit earlier prophetic references before entering the Gospel chapters.
levels.objective: View three promise cards and step into the next archive scene.
levels.uniqueRule: Micah and Malachi are explicitly lookbacks, not newly dated after Nehemiah; the campaign ends at resurrection, before Acts and the epistles.

levels.title: The Announcement
levels.location: Nazareth and Judean-household observation exhibits
levels.storyBeat: Mary’s announcement and visit to Elizabeth begin the arrival arc.
levels.objective: Follow two context paths and view the announcement and visit panels.
levels.uniqueRule: No player makes the incarnation happen, no invented divine dialogue, no targetable angel or miraculous power pickup.

levels.title: Bethlehem at Night
levels.location: town approach, stable-view exhibit and separate travelers’ route
levels.storyBeat: The birth account introduces joy within humble surroundings; Matthew’s visitors are presented in their own context.
levels.objective: Guide three fictional travelers to clear observation routes and view the birth panel.
levels.uniqueRule: Do not assert the magi arrive on the shepherds’ night; no infant combatant, no loot gifts stolen from the scene.

levels.title: The Road to Egypt
levels.location: fictional night-road exercise and family-flight context gallery
levels.storyBeat: The flight into Egypt makes protection urgent while keeping the difficult history restrained.
levels.objective: Lead Ken through three guarded route checkpoints without engaging optional pursuers.
levels.uniqueRule: The historical family is narrated, not a damageable escort; violence against children is not playable or graphically shown.

levels.title: A Voice by the Jordan
levels.location: Jordan riverbank and baptism observation path
levels.storyBeat: John’s ministry prepares the way and Jesus’ baptism marks a new beginning.
levels.objective: Visit three context stations and reach the river viewpoint.
levels.uniqueRule: No baptism mini-game buys stats or salvation; no playable depiction of God or the Spirit as a weapon.

levels.title: The Wilderness Choice
levels.location: wilderness context panels and a quiet return route
levels.storyBeat: Jesus’ temptation is a fixed account; David reflects on strength used without domination.
levels.objective: Pair three temptation-and-response context panels and leave by the marked path.
levels.uniqueRule: Jesus is not a selectable fighter; Satan is not a sword-fight boss defeated by David, and the narrative outcome cannot change.

levels.title: Follow on the Shore
levels.location: Galilean shore, fishing platforms and boat-view exhibit
levels.storyBeat: The disciples’ call begins a chapter of learning and companionship.
levels.objective: Cross three shore routes and gather ordinary model-net supplies.
levels.uniqueRule: The catch and call remain narrated; the player’s fishing success never manufactures the miracle.

levels.title: The Mountain Teaching
levels.location: hillside paths and teaching context stations
levels.storyBeat: The teaching shifts David’s idea of greatness from defeating rivals toward character and care.
levels.objective: Match four illustrated situations with clearly labeled original summaries of the teaching.
levels.uniqueRule: No invented sayings attributed to Jesus; failure gives another try, never a holiness score or lost salvation.

levels.title: The Road of Mercy
levels.location: parable exercise on a desert road with three safe bays
levels.storyBeat: The Good Samaritan parable invites the friends to cross their own boundaries of compassion.
levels.objective: Clear three fictional bandit waves and carry supplies to the protected traveler.
levels.uniqueRule: Label the scene Parable exercise; the Samaritan is a positive neighbor, not an enemy faction. The injured person cannot be damaged by combat.

levels.title: The Storm on the Lake
levels.location: boat-model deck and distant storm observation panels
levels.storyBeat: Fear rises on the lake; the account’s calming comes through Jesus’ action.
levels.objective: Secure three model-deck stations and reach Ken’s safe bay.
levels.uniqueRule: The storm ends on the narrative cue, not when the player fills a power bar; no weather boss or Jesus damage animation.

levels.title: Five Loaves and Two Fish
levels.location: hillside crowd routes and basket preparation bays
levels.storyBeat: Need meets compassion; the friends help organize a fictional crowd exercise.
levels.objective: Carry five model loaves and two model fish to the preparation station and open two walking lanes.
levels.uniqueRule: Do not make the player generate multiplied food through combos; the feeding is fixed narrated miracle and supplies are educational models.

levels.title: Across the Water
levels.location: boat viewpoint and clearly fictional stone-step archive route
levels.storyBeat: The water account puts trust and fear side by side, leading toward recognition.
levels.objective: Cross three marked archive stepping routes and reach the boat observation panel.
levels.uniqueRule: The player does not walk on water through a faith meter; Peter and Jesus’ account is shown separately without alternate rescue outcomes.

levels.title: Through the Roof
levels.location: house-model roof paths and street-side observation bay
levels.storyBeat: Friends carry a paralytic to Jesus; companionship becomes practical work.
levels.objective: Coordinate three stretcher-model lifts and open the observation route.
levels.uniqueRule: The model passenger is invulnerable; lifting is cooperation, not a healing mechanic. Jesus’ healing is fixed narration.

levels.title: The Way Home
levels.location: parable road, farm threshold and home courtyard
levels.storyBeat: The prodigal-son parable gives Ken space to ask about return and forgiveness.
levels.objective: Find three context markers and choose the route home without a combat detour.
levels.uniqueRule: Label the scene as a parable; do not make the father an unlockable boss or forgiveness a purchasable reward.

levels.title: Above the Crowd
levels.location: Jericho street routes and a sycamore-view platform
levels.storyBeat: Zacchaeus’ encounter links welcome with a changed response.
levels.objective: Climb two observation routes and guide three crowd groups to safe lanes.
levels.uniqueRule: No robbing NPCs for coins or buying a better moral score; the tree is ordinary scenery and Jesus is not controlled by the player.

levels.title: The Call at Bethany
levels.location: Bethany approach, tomb-view path and quiet gathering space
levels.storyBeat: Lazarus’ death and Jesus’ raising of him deepen the chapter’s hope before Jerusalem.
levels.objective: Follow three context stations and watch the restrained account scene.
levels.uniqueRule: No necromancy spell, resurrection resource, targetable corpse or player timing that causes the raising.

levels.title: The Road into Jerusalem
levels.location: Jerusalem approach with broad crowd lanes
levels.storyBeat: The entry into Jerusalem carries joy and approaching sorrow together.
levels.objective: Open three crowd routes and guide Ken to the observation terrace.
levels.uniqueRule: No mount racing that controls Jesus’ entry, no crushing crowds for points, and no forced interpretation of every passerby.

levels.title: Teaching in the Courts
levels.location: temple-court observation path and teaching gallery
levels.storyBeat: Debates and warnings prepare the story’s final chapter; David listens before reaching for a weapon.
levels.objective: Visit three teaching-context stations and exit to the supper chapter.
levels.uniqueRule: No arena duel inside worship space; the temple-cleansing account is contextualized without turning Jesus into a brawler or stereotyping Jewish people.

levels.title: Bread and the Cup
levels.location: upper-room observation exhibit and service table
levels.storyBeat: The Last Supper begins the finale through fellowship, service and the approaching betrayal.
levels.objective: Arrange ordinary exhibit supplies, view the service and supper panels, and continue with Ken.
levels.uniqueRule: No sacrament stat potion, timed Eucharist mini-game, invented promises spoken as Jesus, or targetable apostle.

levels.title: Weapons Put Away
levels.location: garden path, distant arrest view and safe observation bay
levels.storyBeat: Gethsemane moves from prayer to arrest; David’s action button becomes Help and Listen.
levels.objective: Walk beside Ken, close the weapon satchel and view the arrest context.
levels.uniqueRule: No fight that prevents the arrest or rewards harming guards; include the restraint and healing context from Luke 22:49-51.

levels.title: The Courtyard at Night
levels.location: courtyard observation route and quiet outer street
levels.storyBeat: Peter’s denial is fixed history; Ken recognizes his own fear and the need for mercy.
levels.objective: Visit three context markers and leave with Ken through the quiet route.
levels.uniqueRule: The player cannot force Peter’s denial or rewrite it through dialogue options; no score condemns a character as beyond forgiveness.

levels.title: At the Cross
levels.location: restrained distant cross viewpoint and mourners’ path
levels.storyBeat: The death of Jesus is presented with solemnity and care; the friends have no victory move for this moment.
levels.objective: Reach the viewpoint, view the account with captions and continue to the burial.
levels.uniqueRule: No crucifixion controls, nails as collectibles, gore, fight against Jesus, revenge battle, damage bar or alternate death outcome.

levels.title: The Quiet Tomb
levels.location: garden tomb approach, stone path and sunset rest point
levels.storyBeat: Burial leaves the friends waiting in grief rather than filling the silence with a battle.
levels.objective: Walk three short observation paths and place an ordinary journal marker at the rest point.
levels.uniqueRule: No loot from the tomb, timed burial score, grave combat or mechanic that manufactures the resurrection.

levels.title: Dawn at the Empty Tomb
levels.location: garden dawn, open-tomb observation and reunion path
levels.storyBeat: The resurrection announcement turns grief toward hope; David and Ken finish their journey ready to serve their neighbors.
levels.objective: Explore the dawn garden, view the Gospel-context panels and meet Ken at the final overlook.
levels.uniqueRule: Keep each Gospel’s details attributed to that account; no boss resurrection, combat Jesus, resurrection spell, faith currency or scored theological test.
